title: School council
situation: An international school is changing its curriculum. The head (AmE: principal) wants to cut coding and essay writing: “AI can do all that now.”

for: You need to understand code to check what AI writes — **that's where you really add value**.
**It was a steep learning curve**, but it taught me to think step by step.
against: **They're handing it over to AI** — why spend years on it at school?
Lots of tech companies **have stopped hiring juniors**, so why train kids for jobs that may not be there?

for: It's **more important than you'd think** — writing helps you sort out your thoughts.
When AI writes the first draft, I edit it — **that's where I really add value**.
against: **They're handing it over to AI** — nobody writes reports from scratch any more.
We did essay writing every week, and **I've never used it since**.

for: **You never know when it might come in handy** — I never thought I'd live abroad.
Translation apps **only get you so far** — try making friends through one.
against: AI translates everything now — **what's the point of** six years of French?
I did French at school, but when I moved to France, **I had to start from scratch**.

for: It's **more important than you'd think** — people judge you by your spelling.
**You never know when it might come in handy** — when your battery dies, for example.
against: It's **a complete waste of time** — spellcheck does it for us.
**It's out of date.** Nobody writes by hand any more.

for: It's **more useful than you'd think** — in shops, with discounts, when you split a bill.
It was hard, but it paid off — I notice at once when a bill doesn't look right.
against: **What's the point of** mental maths when everyone has a phone?
We spent hours on it, and **I've never used it since**.

for: **They're handing** more and more work **over to AI**, so someone has to check it.
**I learned that the hard way** — kids shouldn't have to.
against: The tools change every month, so what they learn will be **out of date** by the time they leave school.
Kids **pick it up** on their own — and very fast.

for: Everything goes **out of date**, so **you need to adapt** — and that means knowing how to learn.
When I changed careers, **I had to start from scratch**, and nobody had ever shown me how to learn.
against: **I picked it up on the job** — you learn how to learn by doing it, not in a lesson.
**School only gets you so far** — everyone learns differently, so you have to find your own way.

for: AI makes things up, so checking the facts — **that's where you really add value**.
Before I believe a big news story, **I read up on it** — kids should learn to do that too.
against: **What's the point of** a separate subject? Every teacher can do it in their lessons.
You just **do your homework** before you share something — that's a habit, not a subject.

for: My first year as a manager **was a steep learning curve** — nobody had ever taught me how to deal with people.
**I had to learn the hard way**, and I'd love my kids to have it easier.
against: **School only gets you so far** — you learn it from real people, not from role-plays.
It's **more complicated than you'd think** — every difficult person is different, so a school course can't really prepare you.

for: A lot of companies **have stopped hiring juniors**, so young people get fewer chances to learn teamwork at work — school has to do it.
It's **more important than you'd think** — even a team of clever people gets nowhere if they can't work together.
against: They already do group projects all the time — **what's the point of** a whole subject?
**I picked it up on the job** — you can't learn it from a textbook.
